sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: This creeping or climbing perennial grows on sandy or gravelly beaches and dunes in temperate and circumpolar regions. Its stems can reach about 1.5 m.

sections.title: Leaves, flowers and pods
sections.text: The leaves usually bear several pairs of leaflets and end in a tendril. The pea-shaped flowers are violet to purple and produce pods containing seeds.

sections.title: Food use
sections.text: Food uses of the leaves and seeds are reported, but a University of Alaska source classifies the species as edible with cautions. These sources do not establish a safe preparation or amount, so this is not a foraging recommendation.
